slides.title: What an agent is, and how it differs from a chat
slides.text: In a chat, AI can only do one thing: write text into a box. It tells you what it would do, proposes, drafts, advises. The arm that touches the world is you: you copy, you paste, you press send. Between what the AI decides and what happens to your files, your money, or your clients, there's a person (you) also watching. An agent is the same thing with that gap removed. The doubt that'll come up here is whether an…

slides.title: Practice: Classify what you're already using, in one minute
slides.text: Before touching any settings. Open a new chat and paste the message below, filling in the list with the AI tools you actually use, not the ones you've just heard of. Write three or four: it could be "ChatGPT on my phone," "Claude on the web," "the assistant built into Gmail," "Copilot inside Word." The goal isn't to pass a test, it's for you to stop treating things that can do very different things to you as if they…

slides.title: Giving it tools so it can do things
slides.text: A language model only knows how to produce text, and giving it a tool doesn't give it hands: it gives it a form it can fill out. Instead of answering you "you've got three open slots Thursday," it writes an internal note that says "call read_calendar with date 2026-09-03" and goes quiet, waiting. That note gets picked up by the program wrapped around it — the Claude app, ChatGPT's, Gemini's — and it's that program…

slides.title: Practice: Inventory the doors you already have open
slides.text: Before connecting anything, check what's already connected, which surprises a lot of people. In Claude: click your name or initials at the bottom left, go into "Settings," and find the "Connectors" tab. In ChatGPT: click your name bottom left, "Settings," and find "Apps & Connectors." You'll see two lists: connected and available. Write down on paper how many you have connected and which ones. If there's one you…

slides.title: MCP: connecting your programs to the AI
slides.text: Right now you already connect things to the AI every day, just by hand. You open a document, select three paragraphs, copy them, paste them into the chat. You're the cable. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is the technical agreement that removes that human cable. With MCP, the program storing your data and the program running the AI talk to each other directly. They talk in a language both sides understand. Anthropic…

items: In the Claude or ChatGPT app, in a computer browser

A screen with cards or rows, each with an application's name and logo. The ones not set up carry a "Connect" button. The ones that are usually show marked, at the top, or with a button that says "Disconnect" instead of "Connect."

slides.title: Skills: procedures that trigger themselves
slides.text: A skill is a folder with a text file inside it. That file is called SKILL.md and contains a procedure of yours written in plain English: when to use it, what data is needed, the steps in order, how you know it came out right, and what's never done. There's no code, no programming, nothing to install on your computer. It's literally the manual you'd hand someone starting work with you on Monday. The difference from…

slides.title: Practice: Pull the procedure you repeat most out of your head
slides.text: Before writing any file, pick a procedure: something you do at least once a week, always the same steps, and that's a pain to repeat. Quotes, replies to bad reviews, product listings, meeting summaries, replies to the same type of email. Pick the one you did the most this month, not the flashiest one. Then paste the prompt below, swapping in the brackets, and answer the questions one at a time, with real numbers.…
items: In the Claude or ChatGPT app, in a new conversation

A ten- or fifteen-minute conversation ending in a numbered procedure you recognize as yours, plus a short list of gaps to fill in. If reading it you think "this could apply to anyone," you're not done.

slides.title: What would prevent your project from being handed off?
slides.text: Use one case you actually observed. Name the evidence, the risk and the next check. There is no automatically correct option for this open question.

Unreliable repeated event
Unknown permission
No recovery owner
